source: Daily ruling reasons compiled by Claude from same-day news reports (CNBC, CNN, AP, Bloomberg, Reuters, TheStreet, Quartz, Benzinga). Week in review: index closes from AP; sector and bond (TLT) changes from IBKR weekly closes of the SPDR sector ETFs; gold, oil from Stock Rover; 10-year from AP; VIX and Bitcoin are late-day readings (Vistap Global) and approximate. Nasdaq Composite shown in place of the Nasdaq 100 this week because IBKR index data was unavailable and no verified Nasdaq 100 close was found

ruling_reasons.text: Memory-chip stocks slumped on news of advances by Chinese memory maker ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT); the Dow rose more than 195 points but the S&P 500 and Nasdaq closed lower

Memory-chip selloff spread from Asia: South Korea's Kospi fell 5.5%, SK Hynix −10.1%, Samsung −7.4% on CXMT competition fears; in early U.S. trading Micron fell about 5% and storage names Western Digital, Seagate and Sandisk 6–7%

Mixed big-bank earnings: JPMorgan missed ($5.57 vs $5.90 per share expected), a rare miss, but recovered after raising 2026 net interest income guidance to $106.2B; Goldman rose about 3.5% on dealmaking and trading, Wells Fargo lagged
Rotation rather than a selloff: S&P 500 closed near flat as banks and the Dow gained while chips dragged the Nasdaq; rising energy costs ahead of the September CPI report kept investors cautious

Late-session recovery: New York Fed President John Williams said one more rate hike looks appropriate this year but he sees no need for further tightening in 2027; Treasuries rallied (yields fell) and the S&P 500 closed little changed near its record
Stock futures flat overnight as traders wait for September CPI (8:30 a.m. New York, 20:30 Singapore), the week's biggest release; the S&P 500 and Nasdaq-100 had slipped for a second straight session

Hot September CPI: prices rose 3.7% from a year earlier versus 3.6% expected, up from 3.4% in August and the highest since May (0.6% on the month, as expected); core inflation also came in above forecasts. Bets on another Fed hike jumped, with October hike odds briefly near 50% before fading

AI-led selloff: S&P 500 −1.11% to 7,718.94 and Nasdaq Composite −1.88%, both their worst day since July and the S&P's first 1% drop in 54 sessions. Debt-heavy AI infrastructure hit hardest (CoreWeave −15%+, Oracle about −9%, Nvidia and AMD lower; chip ETF down a 7th straight day) on worries that higher rates raise the cost of the data-center buildout. Money rotated into health care, staples and energy, keeping the Dow nearly flat

TSMC posted a record profit for a sixth straight quarter, beating estimates on AI demand (analysts had expected net profit up about 65% to roughly NT$746 billion); a key test for chip stocks after a seven-day slide, the CXMT scare and Wednesday's AI selloff

Global AI-hardware rout deepened despite TSMC's beat: Korea's Kospi plunged 7.7% to 5,548.78 (about 21% below its September high, a bear market; trading was halted for 20 minutes), with SK Hynix −11.4% and Samsung −9.5%; Japan's Nikkei −4.8% and SoftBank −9.4%. Drivers: fear of more Fed hikes after the hot CPI, plus worries over the cost of financing the AI build-out. Nvidia, AMD and Micron fell in U.S. trading

Bitcoin fell about 3% to near $81,000 after briefly touching $80,000 in Asian trade: the hot CPI pushed October Fed-hike odds above 50%, about $483 million of leveraged Bitcoin and Ether futures positions were liquidated (mostly longs), and U.S. spot Bitcoin and Ether ETFs saw about $391 million of outflows on 14 Oct. $80,000 is the support level traders are watching
ruling_reasons.source: CoinDesk, CoinGlass, SoSoValue via crypto.news, CoinGape, CryptoTimes

ruling_reasons.text: Second hot inflation read: September wholesale prices (PPI) jumped 1.3% on the month versus 0.5% expected and 6.3% from a year earlier versus 5.3% expected, which CNBC called the biggest annual gain since 2022. Retail sales rose 0.8%, beating forecasts of about 0.3%, and jobless claims stayed low at 199,000. Together they strengthen the case for another Fed hike at the 27–28 October meeting; before the release, Treasury yields had fallen sharply and the dollar had given back its CPI gains
ruling_reasons.source: CNBC, BLS data via ChainCatcher, Schwab, FXStreet

ruling_reasons.text: U.S. open: the S&P 500 slid as tech shares fell for a second day, with the hot wholesale-inflation (PPI) reading adding to rate-hike worries; meanwhile the 10-year Treasury yield held near 5.05%, well below Tuesday's 5.22%, as bond buyers focused on equity and AI-credit stress (closing figures to follow)
ruling_reasons.source: CNBC live updates; yield from IBKR (CBOE TNX)

ruling_reasons.text: Close: stocks recovered from the early PPI scare as Treasury yields fell sharply. Dow +1.1% to 52,177.69, S&P 500 +0.3% to 7,744.06, Nasdaq +0.1% to 26,713.03; health care led and rate-sensitive financials and discretionary bounced. CoreWeave rebounded after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said its cost of capital is falling
ruling_reasons.source: Zacks via Yahoo Finance, Schwab, CNN

ruling_reasons.text: Mixed open (S&P +0.19%, Nasdaq −0.24%, Russell 2000 +1.4%) turned into a tech rout: Fed Chair Warsh declined to rule out an October hike after the hot CPI and PPI, and the Fed enters its blackout period ahead of the 27–28 October FOMC

AI-debt fear returned: CoreWeave −12% (about −25% on the week) as its unsecured 2032 bonds trade below 80 cents and total debt tops $51B; peer Nebius also −12%. Chip stocks fell an 8th–9th straight day, the longest slide since 2008 per Bloomberg; the SOX index −3.8% Friday and −11.4% on the week, its worst since April 2025

Memory names hit again on CXMT competition fears: Seagate −7.5%, Western Digital −6.9%, Sandisk −6.9%, Micron −5.6%; AMD −6.0%, Intel −5.8%. Selling spread to software and cybersecurity: Twilio −10.7%, Okta −8.9%, DigitalOcean −8.7%, software ETF IGV −4.8%

Oil shock lifted energy: Brent +3.7% to $109.86 (touched $110, first time in months), WTI near $99 (+8% on the week). Energy (XLE +2.5%) led, with utilities and staples also up more than 1%, while tech (XLK −3.0%) and communications lagged

Close: S&P 500 −1.09% to 7,659.44, Nasdaq −2.14% to 26,140.03, Dow −0.34% to 52,002.41, Russell 2000 −1.7% to 2,721.37. Week: Nasdaq −4.48% and S&P −1.95% (both worst since June), Russell −3.0%, Dow +0.67%. A rotation, not a rout: the equal-weight S&P had its best week versus tech since 2009. VIX near 20; 10-year yield 5.09%, down from 5.24% a week earlier

Oversold read (Claude, from IBKR daily bars): SOXX RSI(14) 30.4, 2.7 SD below its 20-day average, volume 2.4–2.6× normal but closed at Friday's low (no reversal yet); CoreWeave RSI 28.9, volume 4–5× (a credit story, so it can stay oversold); Micron RSI 33.3 on only modestly higher volume. Stock Trader's Almanac: after an October pullback, the week after monthly options expiration has tended to be bullish. Risks: Brent above $105, Oct 27–28 hike odds, and short-covering against MNQ shorts
